summary: An item opens only when both clicks of a double-click are on it. Each browser remembers what the last two presses of the mouse in its window landed on (`Presses` in src/finder/views.rs). `press_capture`, a capture-phase listener on the whole window, drawn as the first child of the browser's root, shifts the record on every press, since a press on a dialog or a menu never reaches the browser's own elements; the item handlers (`item_interactions` for list, icons and gallery, the column view's own row handler) and `press_in_empty_space` (src/finder/mod.rs) then say what the press landed on: an item, by its path, or the empty space of the list and icon views. A press the system counts second or later is a double-click only after a press on the same item; after a press on another item or in empty space it is a first click, which selects; after a press on anything else it is left alone and stopped where it lands: nothing is opened, selected or deselected, no box starts, and the keyboard stays where it was. Only that one press is left alone; the click after it is a first click again. The record is forgotten when the browser's tab is hidden (`Workspace::leave_active_tab`, src/workspace.rs) and when its Quick Look window closes (src/finder/quick_look.rs), where the browser hears no presses. docs/manual.md: the Double-click row of "Selecting items".
changelog: A double-click on a dialog's Done or Cancel button, on its close button, or beside the dialog no longer opens the file that was under the pointer. The first click closed the dialog, and the second landed on the files as a double-click. A double-click on a menu item, on a notification's close button, or on the close button of a tab did the same, and over empty space the second click cleared the selection. An item now opens only when both clicks are on it. After a click on another item the second click only selects, and after a click on something that the click took away it does nothing to the files and leaves the keyboard where it was. Clicking on quickly after opening a folder no longer opens what comes under the pointer with every click: each item takes a double-click of its own.
behaviour_changes: Double-click on a dialog's Done, Cancel or close button, or beside the dialog: the second click no longer opens and selects the item under the pointer (all four views), no longer clears the selection over empty space (list and icon views), no longer takes the keyboard to the files (it stays, for example, in the search field), and over a list row's other columns it starts no box when the mouse moves while it is down.

The same after a first click on anything that is not an item or the empty space of the list and icon views: a menu item (a double-click on Copy opened the file under the menu), a notification's close button, a tab's close button when the tab bar goes with it, and by the same rule a list header, a group header, a disclosure triangle, a bar. A second-counted press that then lands on an item or on empty space does nothing.

Only that one click is left alone (changed in review). The next click at that spot, which the system counts third, is a first click: it selects the item, or clears the selection over empty space, and the click after it opens the item. As implemented at first, every further click was ignored until the mouse paused or moved.
A second-counted click on a different item from the one before only selects it (was: opened it). All four views.
A second-counted click on an item after a click in the empty space of the list or icon view only selects (was: opened).

Clicking on after a double-click that opened a folder: the third click selects what came under the pointer and the fourth opens it. Before, every further click opened: four quick clicks went three folders deep.

After the browser's tab was hidden, or its Quick Look window closed, a press counted second or later is left alone once. For Quick Look this matters only where the system counts clicks across windows.

Sloppy double-clicks. First press just beside the item in list or icon empty space, second on it: selects (was: opened). First press on a non-item part within the system's few pixels (the list header above the first row, a group header, a disclosure triangle, the column view's blank area and the 6 pt beside its rows, the blank part of the gallery's strip): the second does nothing (was: opened), the click after it selects, and the next opens.
Column view: a press on a row that is no longer there does nothing. Before, a second-counted one could open the pane's current selection.

Unchanged: a double-click with both clicks on the item in every view, on a folder, on one of several selected items, with a menu open (the press that dismisses a menu reaches the row), Cmd+double-click, the file chooser; a triple click on a file opens it twice. A press that is left alone can still drag the item it is on, which is GPUI's own doing: let go where it was pressed, nothing moves.
docs/manual.md, "Selecting items", Double-click row: says both clicks have to be on the item and what a second click does otherwise.
left_out: The brief's second bullet: a double-click on the scope bar's (i) still opens Search Syntax and closes it again where the dialog doesn't open over the pointer. The second click is on the kit's backdrop, which this guard doesn't reach.

Stray second clicks on what is not an item or empty space still act, as before: over a sidebar row the window goes there, a list header sorts, a group header closes its group, a disclosure triangle opens its folder, a toolbar button is pressed. Not in this brief. A guard for the whole file area can't simply drop every second-counted press whose first went to no item: a double-click on the line at a column's edge, which fits the column, begins on no item either.

The buttons under the file area's message keep the guard they have (`message_button_clicked`). This change also covers the result that comes under such a button, but not the other button, so the guard stays.

Presses in other windows and in native menus are not heard. Only the Quick Look window's closing is handled. With a stale record a stray click there selects the item instead of opening it, or opens it if it is the very item last clicked in that browser; never worse than before. Forgetting on every change of the window's active state was considered and left: on macOS GPUI reports that change from a task of its own, which may run after the click that brought the window forward, and the first click of a double-click on an inactive window would then be forgotten.

No kept test, only probes: a notification's close button (implementer, and again in review: second click nothing, third selects, fourth opens); split view (review: a click in one pane and a double-click in the other opens; a stray second click on the other pane's item does nothing); a press that dragged nowhere and then a second click (review: opens in all four views); a double-click on an item with a context menu open (review: opens); a scroll or a reload of the list between the two clicks, toolbar menus open, Quick Look open in its own window (implementer).
`cargo clippy --features term` not run: src/term is untouched and no signature it calls changed. Not compiled for macOS or Windows; the change has no cfg-specific code.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

tests/basics.rs: a_double_click_on_a_dialogs_button_does_nothing_to_the_item_under_it (list and icons; in review: also with every item selected, where a click would narrow the selection)

review_fixes: Found with a test and fixed: after a stray second click, every click that followed without a pause or a move was ignored too. `Presses::on_item` returned None without recording anything, so the next press again found that the press before it had landed nowhere in the views. A double-click on Done, then a double-click on the file under the pointer, opened nothing, and went on opening nothing for as long as the clicking went on, which is what people do when a click seems lost. The brief's own risks say double-click must not need a pause. Now only the one press is left alone: it is recorded as `Pressed::LeftAlone`, and the press after it is a first click on an item or in empty space. a_double_click_on_a_dialogs_button_holds_up_no_click_after_it failed on the implementer's commit (nothing selected by the third click) and passes now; the unit test that pinned the old rule is rewritten and the_click_after_one_that_was_left_alone_is_a_first_click is new.

Found with a test and fixed: a stray second click over a list row's other columns (Date Modified, Size, Kind) still started a box. That part of a row has a listener of its own, which runs before the row's, so `begin_marquee` had run by the time the row left the press alone. With the mouse moving 4 points while it was down, the box replaced the selection with the rows it covered. a_second_click_beside_a_dialog_draws_no_box_when_the_mouse_moves failed on the implementer's commit (selected item 030 and 031 in place of item 001). The listener now asks `Presses::is_stray` first, a query that `on_item` and `in_empty_space` share.

Test added to a_double_click_on_a_dialogs_button_does_nothing_to_the_item_under_it: with every item selected, the selection stays whole. It passed already; it pins that the click event of a press that was left alone narrows nothing (`on_click` goes by the system's count).
Harness: `press_and_move` in tests/common/mod.rs takes the click count, for `Ui::nth_drag_points`.
Commit message: the sentence 'The same goes for the clicks that follow it without a pause.' gave way to the two rules above.
notes:
Checked. With the commit's src diff reverse-applied (the implementer's commit a380cf1), 10 of the 11 UI tests fail, each for the reason the brief gives (Open(item 018.txt) under Done, the selection cleared over empty space, the query left at 'item' because the files took the keyboard, Open under a menu item, under a tab's close button, behind Quick Look, Roadmap.md opened by a click after one on notes.txt, a third click going one folder deeper); the guard test passes, as it should. The four unit tests need the new type, so they went with the diff. The two tests added in review failed on the implementer's commit and pass on the trunk commit. One mutation of the review's code (an ignored press in empty space not recorded) fails the second half of a_double_click_on_a_dialogs_button_holds_up_no_click_after_it and the new unit test. The implementer's thirteen mutations I did not run again. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit after the rebase onto 52e7de4: 756 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. Pushed to origin (52e7de4..c0605b6). I looked at the window myself: the Search Syntax dialog over a list of 120 files, with Done across the Name and Date Modified columns of two rows (light), and the icon view in split view (dark); the new element draws nothing and moves nothing.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code and the probes say. (1) A real double-click that no longer opens. A second-counted press opens when the press before it was recorded on the same path, so I looked for first presses that are not recorded. In all four views the item's handler calls `press_on_row` or `press_on_column_row` before anything else; inside an item only the disclosure triangle and the field of a name being edited keep a press to themselves, for both clicks, as before. The press that dismisses a context menu or a toolbar menu reaches the row (probed). The first click on an inactive window is delivered on macOS (GPUI answers acceptsFirstMouse with yes and marks the press first_mouse). `began()` runs once for each press: one listener for each drawn browser in each frame. `forget()` runs only when a tab is left and when the Quick Look window's view is released, and no press on an item does either between the two clicks; Quick Look's window closes by its keys, its Open button and its close button only. Going by the path, a list read again between the clicks is no obstacle. What does change is the sloppy double-click that begins a few pixels off the item (behaviour_changes). (2) Clicks that stop working. That was real: see review_fixes, the first. With the fix `is_stray` can be true for one press only after each press outside the views. (3) A click that was to do nothing changes the selection or moves the keyboard. The box was real: see review_fixes, the second. A press that is left alone is stopped where it lands, so `#content`, which takes the keyboard for any press that reaches it, and the browser's root never hear of it; listeners in the capture phase (a name being edited ends, a menu closes) have run by then, as before. The click event that follows such a press narrows no selection, because `on_click` goes by the system's count (tested in review).

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) Ignore or select. The stray second click does nothing at all, as the brief's test plan asks; the brief's proposal said to treat it as a single click, which would select the file under the button and replace a multiple selection. With a slow double-click speed set in the system, one click on Done and then a deliberate click on the file under the pointer within that time is left alone once; the next click selects. (b) Where a dialog closes at once (Reduce Motion, and the tests), a triple click on Done selects the file under it with the third click. With the 250 ms closing animation the second click of a fast double-click lands on the leaving dialog, which swallows it, and the third is then left alone. (c) Sloppy double-clicks at the edges of an item no longer open (behaviour_changes). The column view is the least forgiving: its rows sit 6 pt in from the pane's edges, and a press there is on no item and in no empty space, where the list and icon views count it as empty space. (d) A first click, as the views count it, that the system counts second or later doesn't narrow a multiple selection when the mouse is let go: after a stray double-click over one of several selected items, the next click there within the system's time changes nothing visible, and the one after opens the item. `on_click` would need the views' count. (e) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows. Whether macOS counts a click in Quick Look's window and the next one in the window behind as a double-click, I could not verify; the forgetting is harmless where it doesn't.

For briefs still to come.
- icon-tile-hit-target: an item's left press has to reach `press_on_row` first thing, as it does in `item_interactions`, and a press in what becomes empty space between tiles has to go through `press_in_empty_space`, which records it. A press that neither records is taken for a press outside the views, and a second-counted press on the icon beside it would then be left alone, where after a recorded press in empty space it selects. The icon halves of a_double_click_on_a_dialogs_button_does_nothing_to_the_item_under_it and of a_double_click_that_closes_a_tab_does_nothing_to_the_tab_behind_it find the item under the button by the bounds of the `tile` element (`item_at`): if those bounds stay and the hit target shrinks, the tests go on passing while the press lands in empty space, so keep the spot on the icon. A double-click whose first press is in a tile's blank margin will select and not open.
- split-active-pane: a press the views leave alone is stopped in the bubble phase where it lands, so a bubble-phase listener on the pane or the workspace never hears it, and the active pane should not follow it anyway. A capture-phase listener hears every press. Each browser's `press_capture` listener hears every press in the window, in the other pane too, with no hit test: it only shifts the record. `Workspace::leave_active_tab` now also calls `forget_presses()`; whatever else hides a browser that goes on living has to call it too.
- restore-session-tabs, tab-drop-and-close: `self.active` may only change after `leave_active_tab`, as in `new_tab` and `select_tab`, or the tab left behind keeps a record of presses it stops hearing. A tab that never showed has an empty record. a_double_click_that_closes_a_tab_does_nothing_to_the_tab_behind_it needs the tab bar to go when one tab is left, so that an icon is where the second tab's close button was; it asserts both.
- column-pane-selection-by-path (lane-f, in progress): the column row's left handler now begins `cx.stop_propagation(); let Some(click_count) = this.press_on_column_row(col, ix, event.click_count) else { return; };` and opens on that `click_count`, not on `event.click_count`. `press_on_column_row` reads `self.columns[col].entries[ix].path`. If the rebase conflicts there, keep both.
- stale-rows-on-place-change: quick_double_clicks_at_one_spot_open_one_item_each double-clicks a folder and expects the third click at that spot to select the folder that came under the pointer and the fourth to open it; the harness lets the listing arrive between the clicks. If the old rows stay on screen and take no clicks while the next place is read, decide what a press on one is: left unrecorded it counts as a press outside the views, and the next second-counted press on a new row is left alone once.
- context-menus-fit: a double-click on an item still opens it with a menu open because the press that dismisses the menu also reaches the row and is recorded there. If a menu comes to swallow that press, the second click is left alone and the third selects.
- quick-look-empty-state: the release observer in `toggle_quick_look_window` has one more line, `this.forget_presses()`; keep it. In `--term` mode Quick Look is a dialog in the same window, and its presses are heard.
- go-to-folder-keyboard, search-settings-hints-steppers, settings-rows-fit, split-view-toolbar-clip, collapsible-sidebar-sections: the tests here need Done (Search Syntax), Cancel (Go to Folder) and the dialog's close button to be over a row of a 200-item list in a window of the default size, and item 030 beside the dialog. Each asserts that first, so a layout change fails at 'Done is over an item' and the like, not for nothing.
- thumbnail-memory, inactive-selection-colour, content-match-highlight, multi-word-highlights, select-all-perf, view-switch-keeps-selection: independent. In src/finder/views.rs `Pressed` and `Presses` sit between `drag_frame` and `tile_size`, `press_capture`, `forget_presses`, `press_on_row` and `press_on_column_row` above `item_interactions`, and five unit tests at the top of `mod tests`.
- type-select-space, adhoc-index-feedback, regex-content-search: `Render for Finder` has `.child(self.press_capture(cx))` as the root's first child, before the row of sidebar and panes. It has to stay first, so that its listener runs before anything in the browser can stop a press in the capture phase.
- every brief with UI tests: in tests/common/mod.rs `press_and_move` has a sixth argument, the click count (1 for a plain press). New: `Ui::nth_click_point(position, nth)` and `Ui::nth_drag_points(start, end, nth)`. `Ui::select` and `Ui::select_also` call `click_row` and go round the record of presses; a real click after them is a first click.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change unless it says otherwise).
- The guard for the buttons under the file area's message (`message_button_clicked`, from empty-state-messages) has the fault that review_fixes describes first: after a double-click on Search This Computer, every quick click on the results is stopped in the capture phase until a click the system counts as first, so a double-click on the result under the pointer opens nothing until the mouse rests or moves. Clearing the flag at the first left press on the file area, whatever its count, would bound it; the press after the stopped one would then be left alone once more by this change's rule, unless the guard records its press as left alone too.
- A double-click on the scope bar's (i) opens Search Syntax and closes it again (the brief's second bullet).
- A second click whose first went to something that the click took away still acts on what is not an item or empty space: a sidebar row, a list header, a group header, a disclosure triangle, a toolbar button.
- A triple click on a file opens it twice.
- The column view has no empty space of its own: a press in a pane's blank area or beside its rows selects nothing and clears nothing, and, new with this change, the second click of a double-click that begins there is left alone.
- `Ui::select` does not select in the column view (it clicks a row of the list's model), so in the column part of a_double_click_beside_a_dialog_does_nothing_to_the_item_there the selection compared is empty before and after. A stray click that selected would still fail it.
